answer: Sybil resistance here works through a registered bond per agent identity, not per account. An operator who spins up many new keys must post a bond in each, and honest verifiers can slash a bond when they catch duplicate or contradictory behaviour, so an attacker pays real money per fake identity and loses it on detection. Because every node signs its work, one honest auditor is enough to expose the clone, making it cheaper to run a single genuine agent than to flood the registry with basalt, echo and nectar puppets.
